title: Hytale Creative Fullbright control through fingerprinted NativeAOT tail dispatch
summary: AtmosphereTool 2.0.1 adds only a Creative Fullbright slider, 0..100, using the native minimum-light setter. Isolated dispatch, bridge, fog regressions, packaging and installation passed. The component is installed, but live NativeAOT/GC behavior and visual verification remain pending; this is experimental, not a validated general hooking technique.
problem_class: A gradual tool control must reuse a native client-only setting with no supported server API
problem_description: User requested Global Fullbright based on the Creative tools feature and explicitly canceled a separate server lighting-command slider. Screen brightness or weather changes would not implement the requested function.
context: Zytale / AtmosphereTool. User authorized the existing client component and automatic game-folder updates after closing Hytale. Fog rendering was already approved and must be preserved.
outputs: same native Creative lighting operation with intermediate minimum values
versioned install bundle and rollback backup
constraints: Only the Creative Fullbright slider; no server fullbright-command UI or lighting changes
No native game code redistribution or on-disk HytaleClient.exe edits
Exact Windows executable fingerprint; local singleplayer only
Do not treat isolated native fixtures as live runtime or visual validation
known_attempts: Arbitrary fragment-light mixing was rejected before delivery because it did not reproduce the native Creative feature.
A server lighting-command bar was prepared but canceled by explicit user steering and removed from active sources and distribution.
Direct calls into managed NativeAOT routines from a file or GL thread were rejected. The authored leaf dispatcher retains the original managed caller and tail-jumps to existing native code.

The initial C fixture failed because an essential VirtualProtect call was inside an assertion disabled by compiler configuration. Explicitly enabling assertions made the complete fixture execute and pass.

solution_versions.description: Add one 0..100 Creative Fullbright slider and use the existing native Creative minimum-light setter through a fingerprinted leaf dispatch at managed world-update call sites; retain original fog rendering.
changes: Interpolate the native minimum from 0.05 to 0.5; the native routine retains its sixteen-level power curve.
Publish one 20-byte atomic local request and debounce 500 ms of slider inactivity before a native chunk rebuild.
Keep the original managed return address and receiver; do not retain managed pointers or call managed functions from the worker/GL thread.
Observe native toggle changes and restore only a still-owned override on lease release; store the requested slider value per world.
Preserve both fog shader hashes and deliver a transactionally installed 2.0.1 ZIP.
advantages: Uses the Creative routine rather than server lighting or screen brightness
No continuous chunk rebuilding or extra per-pixel effect
disadvantages: Live NativeAOT runtime, GC and visual behavior have not yet been verified
Exact-build in-memory native call-site redirection; not an official plugin API
Applying a new value still triggers the native chunk rebuild
Local singleplayer and manual Windows installation only
test_results: Executed x64 fixture passed 101 levels and 10000 unchanged frames without rebuild
Native file debounce and lease expiry passed
Six native fog shader variants and isolated WGL integration passed with zero GL errors
Hytale 0.7.2 / Java 25 isolated production JAR boot and shutdown passed
Local installation checked four hashes and eleven unchanged saved JSON files
Live in-game Creative behavior and visual review pending

transferability: The separation of native feature semantics, exact build checks, coalesced expensive operations and owned restoration is reusable. The dispatch mechanism is experimental and requires independent ABI/GC/live-runtime validation on every target; offsets and compatibility cannot be generalized.
